steps.title: Create the function signature for sortObjectsByKeys
steps.instruction: Create a function named sortObjectsByKeys that takes two parameters: an array of objects and an array of sort keys. The function should return an array.
steps.hint: Start with either 'function sortObjectsByKeys(arr, keys) {' or 'const sortObjectsByKeys = (arr, keys) => {'. Make sure to include the function body with a placeholder return statement.
steps.expectedOutcome: A function named sortObjectsByKeys is declared with two parameters and returns an array.
successCriteria: The function sortObjectsByKeys is defined with two parameters (arr and keys) and returns an array.
steps.feedbackCorrect: Great! You've successfully declared the sortObjectsByKeys function with the correct parameters and return type.
steps.feedbackPartial: You're close! Make sure your function has exactly two parameters (arr and keys) and returns an array.
steps.feedbackWrong: Check the function name, parameters, and return type. It should be named sortObjectsByKeys, take two parameters (arr and keys), and return an array.

steps.title: Create a copy of the input array to avoid mutation
steps.instruction: Inside your sortObjectsByKeys function, create a shallow copy of the input array parameter using either the spread operator or the slice() method.
steps.hint: You can use the spread operator like [...array] or array.slice() to create a new array with the same elements.
steps.expectedOutcome: The function will have a copy of the input array, preventing mutation of the original data.
successCriteria: The function contains a variable that holds a shallow copy of the input array using spread operator or slice().
steps.feedbackCorrect: Great! You've successfully created a copy of the input array, which is important for avoiding side effects.
steps.feedbackPartial: You're on the right track, but make sure you're creating a copy of the array parameter inside the function.
steps.feedbackWrong: Try again. Remember to create a shallow copy of the array parameter using either the spread operator or slice() method.

steps.title: Implement the sort method on the copied array
steps.instruction: Inside your sortObjectsByKeys function, call the sort() method on the copied array and assign the result back to the copy. Use an empty compare function for now (we'll fill it in later).
steps.hint: You can chain .sort() on the array copy and store the result in a variable, or call it directly on the copy.
steps.expectedOutcome: The function will have a copy of the input array with the sort() method called on it, ready for the compare function implementation.
successCriteria: The sort() method is called on the copied array inside the function.
steps.feedbackCorrect: Great! You've added the sort method call. Next, we'll implement the compare function.
steps.feedbackPartial: You're on the right track, but make sure you're calling sort() on the copied array inside the function.
steps.feedbackWrong: Let's focus on calling the sort() method on the array copy. Check the hint if you're stuck.

steps.title: Create the compare function inside sort()
steps.instruction: Inside the sort() call, add a compare function that takes two parameters 'a' and 'b'.
steps.hint: The compare function should be defined directly as an argument to sort(). For example: copy.sort(function(a, b) { /* comparison logic */ })
steps.expectedOutcome: The sort() method now has a compare function that receives two objects 'a' and 'b' as parameters.
successCriteria: The compare function is defined inside sort() with parameters 'a' and 'b'.
steps.feedbackCorrect: Great! You've added the compare function structure. Next we'll implement the multi-key comparison logic.
steps.feedbackPartial: You're close. Make sure you've added a function with two parameters inside the sort() call.
steps.feedbackWrong: The compare function should be defined directly inside sort() with two parameters.

steps.title: Loop through the sort keys array
steps.instruction: Inside the compare function, create a for loop that iterates through each key in the sort keys array. The sort keys array will be passed as a second parameter to the sortObjectsByKeys function.
steps.hint: Use a for loop with a counter variable (like i) to iterate through each element of the sort keys array. You'll need to access the current key using array indexing.
steps.expectedOutcome: The compare function will have a for loop structure that can iterate through each key in the sortKeys array.
successCriteria: A for loop is created inside the compare function that iterates through sortKeys using a counter variable.
steps.feedbackCorrect: Great! You've successfully added the for loop structure that will iterate through each sort key. This is essential for comparing objects by multiple criteria.
steps.feedbackPartial: You're on the right track, but make sure you've created a proper for loop that can iterate through the sortKeys array. Check that you're using the correct syntax with a counter variable and accessing array elements.
steps.feedbackWrong: The for loop structure isn't quite right. Remember to create a for loop that iterates through each element in the sortKeys array using a counter variable like i.

steps.title: Compare values for the current key
steps.instruction: Inside your for loop, get the values for the current key from both objects (a and b) and compare them. Write the comparison logic that will determine the sort order.
steps.hint: Access the property value from each object using bracket notation with the current key, then compare them with standard comparison operators.
steps.expectedOutcome: The compare function now retrieves and compares the values for each sort key, though the loop doesn't yet return the comparison result.
successCriteria: The code inside the for loop accesses a[sortKeys[i]] and b[sortKeys[i]] and includes comparison logic using if statements or the localeCompare method.
steps.feedbackCorrect: Great! You've successfully implemented the value comparison for the current sort key. The compare function now examines the specific properties from both objects.
steps.feedbackPartial: You're on the right track. Make sure you're accessing the correct properties using the current key from the sortKeys array and comparing them with proper comparison operators.
steps.feedbackWrong: The comparison logic is missing or incorrect. Remember to get the values from both objects using the current key and compare them to determine the sort order.

steps.title: Handle ascending/descending sort order
steps.instruction: Inside the for loop, check if the current sort key starts with '-' to determine descending order. If it does, strip the '-' prefix and compare b[key] with a[key] (instead of a[key] with b[key]) to reverse the sort order.
steps.hint: You can use string methods like startsWith() and slice() to check for and remove the '-' prefix from the key.
steps.expectedOutcome: The compare function now handles both ascending (default) and descending (indicated by '-') sort orders for each key.
successCriteria: The code checks if the sort key starts with '-', strips it if present, and compares values with reversed order for descending sorts.
steps.feedbackCorrect: Great! You've successfully implemented the logic to handle ascending and descending sort orders based on the key prefix.
steps.feedbackPartial: You're on the right track. Make sure you're checking for the '-' prefix, stripping it when present, and reversing the comparison order for descending sorts.
steps.feedbackWrong: The implementation doesn't yet handle descending sort orders. Review how to detect the '-' prefix and reverse the comparison.

steps.title: Return comparison result for current key
steps.instruction: Inside the for loop, after comparing values for the current key, add logic to return -1, 0, or 1 if the values are not equal.
steps.hint: Compare the two values for the current key. If they're different, return -1 if a should come before b, or 1 if b should come before a. If they're equal, continue to the next key.
steps.expectedOutcome: The compare function will now return a comparison result when values differ for a key, allowing the sort to work properly.
successCriteria: Comparison logic returns -1, 0, or 1 based on value comparison
Return statement is inside the for loop
steps.feedbackCorrect: Great! You've added the comparison logic that returns the proper sort order when values differ.
steps.feedbackPartial: You're on the right track, but make sure you're returning -1, 0, or 1 based on the comparison of values for the current key.
steps.feedbackWrong: The comparison logic is missing or incorrect. You need to compare the values for the current key and return -1, 0, or 1.

steps.title: Handle equal values and continue to next key
steps.instruction: Inside the for loop, after comparing values for the current key, add logic to continue to the next key if the values are equal. If all keys are equal, return 0 at the end of the compare function.
steps.hint: After your comparison logic, use an if statement to check if the values are not equal. If they are not equal, return the comparison result. If they are equal, let the loop continue to the next key. After the loop, return 0 to indicate all keys were equal.
steps.expectedOutcome: The compare function now properly handles equal values by continuing to the next sort key, and returns 0 only when all keys are equal.
successCriteria: The compare function includes logic to continue to the next key when values are equal, and returns 0 after the loop if all keys were equal.
steps.feedbackCorrect: Great! You've successfully implemented the logic to handle equal values and continue to the next key. This completes the core multi-key sorting algorithm.
steps.feedbackPartial: You're on the right track, but make sure you're handling both cases: returning the comparison result when values differ, and continuing the loop when they're equal. Also don't forget to return 0 after the loop.
steps.feedbackWrong: The compare function doesn't yet handle equal values correctly. Review the example: when values are equal, the loop should continue to the next key. When all keys are equal, return 0.

steps.title: Return the sorted array
steps.instruction: After the sort() call, return the sorted copy of the array from the sortObjectsByKeys function.
steps.hint: Add a return statement at the end of your function to return the sorted array.
steps.expectedOutcome: The sortObjectsByKeys function will return the sorted array when called.
successCriteria: The sortObjectsByKeys function returns the sorted copy array.
steps.feedbackCorrect: Great! Your function now returns the sorted array, completing the implementation.
steps.feedbackPartial: You're close. Make sure you're returning the sorted array from the function.
